# Code review: CI quality gate moved into a reusable workflow

Mode: explicit range `0056b6d5c...HEAD`, full pipeline, with a subagent limit of 2 (the only allowed deviation). Nothing was modified, installed, run or posted.

**Scope:** 6 files, +325 −249 · base `0056b6d` → `d10e515` (1 commit: "ci: Extract the quality gate into a reusable workflow")
**Profile:** safe-client-gateway · GitHub Actions YAML plus agent docs · 10 non-negotiables in AGENTS.md, plus the "no stale guides" and SPDX rules from `reviewing.md` · 7 of 9 areas have surface

## Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | Fix the two stale doc lines, then open the PR |
| **Score** | **93 / 100** (adjudicated 1 of 4) |
| **Held down by** | Docs describe `staging.yml` and `production.yml`, which don't exist yet |
| **Fix first** | `docs/agents/testing.md:36`, `docs/agents/commits-and-prs.md:166` |

## Scores by area (worst first)

| Area | Score | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Conventions | 85 | Stale guides (P2), a comment split in half |
| Regression | 90 | Deploy gate is wider than the commit message says |
| KISS | 95 | Three inputs that no caller sets |
| Security | 100 | Checked `secrets: inherit`, `permissions`, and fork-PR secret exposure: nothing new |
| Bugs | 100 | Moved job bodies are identical to the old ones, apart from the input substitutions |
| Architecture | 100 | One definition with two entry points; the reusable declares no `concurrency` (so no caller/callee deadlock) |
| Performance | 100 | PR cancel-on-supersede is kept (`pull-request.yml:23-25`) |
| DRY | 100 | Duplicated `services:` blocks existed before and were only moved |
| Testing | n/a | No test surface for workflows. `actionlint` isn't installed, so the YAML wasn't statically checked |

## What this review did not cover
- Branch protection lives outside the repo. The required-check names were taken from the commit message.
- GitHub Actions behaviour (how reusable workflows report success, how skipped jobs count) comes from platform semantics. No live run was observed.
- `.git/safe-code-review/last-run.tsv` is from a different diff (base `8be0434`), so there's no "since your last run" comparison. It wasn't overwritten, because this review was read-only.

## Fix before opening

**CNV-001 · P2 · Docs describe workflows that don't exist**
- `docs/agents/testing.md:36` says `_ci-node.yml` is "called by `pull-request.yml`, `staging.yml` and `production.yml`".
- `docs/agents/commits-and-prs.md:166` says "the build and deploy jobs live in `staging.yml` and `production.yml`".
- Neither file exists at HEAD. `.github/workflows/` holds `_ci-node.yml`, `ci.yml`, `pull-request.yml` and three unrelated workflows. Build and deploy are still in `ci.yml:39-136`, and the commit message itself says the billing README keeps pointing at `ci.yml` "until the next PR".
- **Why it matters:** anyone following these guides (people or agents) goes looking for files that aren't there. This breaks the "no stale guides" rule in `reviewing.md`.
- **Fix:** describe the state at HEAD: callers are `pull-request.yml` and `ci.yml`, and build/deploy is in `ci.yml`. Update the text when the follow-up PR adds those files.
- Confidence 90. Verified directly and not adjudicated, so it counts at full weight.

## Worth a ticket or a quick fix

**REG-001 · P3 · Deploy is now gated on more jobs than before** (validator: PARTIAL, refuter: STANDS → confirmed with narrower scope, confidence 60)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:44` and `:81` changed from `needs: [biome, tests-finish]` (old lines 275 and 312) to `needs: [ci]`, which waits for the whole reusable workflow.
- On a push to main, a failure in `license-headers` or `env-validation` now blocks `docker-publish-staging` and `autodeploy`. Before this change, staging still deployed.
- On a release, only `env-validation` is newly blocking. `license-headers` is skipped on release events (`_ci-node.yml:35`), and a skipped job doesn't fail the caller.
- This contradicts the commit message: "Nothing about building or deploying changes here."
- **Fix:** either say so in the PR body (a stricter gate is arguably what you want), or keep the old gate by listing jobs explicitly.

| ID | Pri | Where | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| CNV-002 | P3 | `.github/workflows/_ci-node.yml:277` | The move split a comment. "Production runs on arm64 only… We run on an" now dangles at the end of the reusable, and its second half was deleted. `ci.yml:39` lost the arm64 explanation above `docker-publish-staging`. Move the full two-line comment back to `ci.yml:39`. |
| KIS-001 | P3 | `.github/workflows/_ci-node.yml:17-29` | No caller passes the `node_version`, `python_version` or `ref` inputs (`ci.yml:35-37`, `pull-request.yml:27-30`). `ref` also reaches the `license-headers` diff logic, which assumes HEAD is the triggering commit. Either drop the inputs until a caller needs them, or say which upcoming PR uses them. The `# Krypton` comments at :82, :100, :164 and :234 are now misleading next to a parameterised version. |

## Needs action when this merges (not scored; you already flagged it)
The required checks `tests (test:cov)`, `tests-finish` and `biome` will report as `ci / …`. Branch protection has to be updated at merge time, or every open PR in the repo blocks. Consider putting this at the top of the PR body, not only in the commit message.

## Your call

| ID | Options |
|---|---|
| CNV-001 | fix now (recommended) |
| REG-001 | fix, or document it in the PR body |
| CNV-002 / KIS-001 | fix now, or skip |

## Worth tidying
There's nothing to propose beyond the findings. Left alone: the duplicated redis/postgres/rabbitmq `services:` blocks in `_ci-node.yml:126-157` and `:194-227`. They existed before this change, and I found no YAML-anchor pattern in the repo to point to as the model.

## Ruled out
- **`secrets: inherit` on `pull_request`:** pull-request workflows already run the PR's own workflow files with the same secret access, and fork PRs get no secrets. Nothing gets worse.
- **SPDX headers:** present on all 6 files.
- **The `license-headers` `if:` guard inside the reusable:** `github.event_name` is the caller's event, so it behaves exactly as before.
- **`concurrency` on `ci.yml:19-21`:** now only covers main and release refs, and main still isn't cancelled.

## How this was produced
- Scope and profile were done by hand. I ran all seven category passes myself, per your 2-subagent limit.
- One finding (REG-001) went to adjudication, using one validator and one refuter. The other three count at full weight, unadjudicated.
- The job bodies were checked for equivalence by diffing old `ci.yml` lines 33-269 against `_ci-node.yml` lines 33-277. The only differences are the input substitutions and the split comment.
